sources.title: Earliest tea as evidence for one branch of the Silk Road — Scientific Reports

notes: 神农尝百草等传说把饮茶推到远古，但缺乏实证。浙江田螺山等遗址的茶树栽培说仍有争议；目前较扎实的实物是西安等地西汉茶遗存，而陆羽《茶经》则标志唐代饮茶习俗的经典化。印度阿萨姆亦有独立驯化线索，故起源地与最早年代均存争议。
notes_en: Legends (for example Shennong) push tea drinking into deep antiquity without hard evidence. Claims of Neolithic cultivation at sites such as Tianluoshan remain debated. The firmest early physical tea is Western Han material from Xi’an; Lu Yu’s Cha Jing marks Tang classicization. Separate Assam domestication lines also complicate a single-origin story.
summary_zh: 茶树原产东亚；西汉西安一带已有茶的实物证据，唐代陆羽《茶经》推动饮茶普及。最早驯化年代与地点仍有争议。
summary_en: Tea is native to East Asia. Western Han remains from Xi’an are early physical evidence; Lu Yu’s Tang Classic of Tea popularized drinking. Domestication date and place remain disputed.
